notes: Machine-readable twin of INSTALL.md. Keep both in sync. status values: documented = commands taken from the repo README; unverified = taken from vendor docs or search results, never run on the host; planned = not available yet. Release assets (the plugin archive, the .mcpb, the DeepSeek Harness package and the add-on) are built by .github/workflows/release.yml; a route that uses one is only usable once a published release lists it. first_run and keys describe the setup tools: setup_status (what works now) and open_setup (the masked key page); both are in the runtime bundle, the .mcpb and a source build.

after_install.description: Source route only. dist/ folders are build output and are not in git, so every route that installs from the repository must build once. Skip this when runtime/bundle/index.mjs exists (release archive).
after_install.locate_plugin_root: The folder that contains scripts/bootstrap.mjs and .mcp.json. Search for it; do not guess.

first_run.description: Owns first-run: detects the app, follows the route for it in this file, calls setup_status, opens the key page only when a key is wanted, re-checks, and ends with a tiny real search.
first_run.status_shape: Three groups, works_now, needs_you and optional, each item with Chinese and English text. rendered.zh and rendered.en hold the text to show. Chinese is the default.
first_run.smoke_test: uv run literature-research/scripts/literature_search.py review --question "setup check" --pubmed-query "CRISPR base editing[Title]" --limit 3 --top-n 3 --output <private-temp>/ai4s-setup-check

keys.rule: Never in chat and never in a command or tool argument. Optional: search needs no key. Ask only for a key that unlocks something the user asked for.
keys.tool_arguments: keys: the keys to offer, in order (omit for all three); language: zh or en
keys.tool_result: opened (whether the browser was launched), url (no code in it), keys, message; fallback_code only when opened is false
keys.if_browser_not_opened: Give the user url and fallback_code to type into the page.
keys.if_tool_missing_or_failing: Double-click Setup AI4S.bat (Windows) or Setup AI4S.command (Mac) in the archive folder. Only if that fails, give one line: node runtime/bundle/index.mjs --setup (runtime/dist/index.js on a source build), after saying how to open a terminal in the plugin folder.
keys.takes_effect: PubMed and EasyScholar keys are read on the next search. A Zotero key takes effect after the app restarts; setup_status says so.
keys.developer_only: scripts/onboard.mjs. Never mention it to a beginner.

workbuddy.label: WorkBuddy
steps: add the GitHub repository as a plugin marketplace through the WorkBuddy interface
workbuddy.fallback: Add the two MCP servers from .mcp.json to ~/.workbuddy/mcp.json (no leading dot before workbuddy), using absolute paths.

claude-desktop.label: Claude Desktop
steps: download the .mcpb from the releases page
double-click it, or drag it onto the Claude Desktop window
leave the two optional settings as they are, or fill in the Zotero key in the masked field
claude-desktop.covers: Zotero tools only. Not the three skills and not the full-text tools.
claude-desktop.note: Built and validated with the mcpb CLI by CI; not yet installed in Claude Desktop, and the Node version it ships is unconfirmed (the bundle asks for 22.13 or newer). If the releases page does not list the file, say so. The key page is also available through open_setup.

deepseek-harness.label: DeepSeek Harness
steps: download the .tgz from the releases page
DeepSeek Harness: Plugins page, Add plugin, paste the path of the downloaded file
Keys and Check at the end
deepseek-harness.done_by: The user. The Plugins page is the one install step an agent cannot do.
deepseek-harness.no_build: The package carries the prebuilt tools, so after_install does not apply. No separate Node.js is needed: the tools run on DeepSeek Harness's own Node, which for Desktop is unconfirmed.
deepseek-harness.covers: The Zotero tools (19), the full-text tools (6) and all four skills. Tools appear as mcp__ai4s-literature-zotero__<tool> and mcp__ai4s-literature-fulltext__<tool>.
deepseek-harness.command_line: dsh plugin --profile desktop add <path to the .tgz>, with Desktop closed; dsh needs Node.js 22.19 or newer and exits without installing on older versions. Tried with dsh web 0.2.1-rc.2 (profile web) on macOS and checked by CI on Linux; the profile name desktop comes from the vendor docs and is untried.
not_yet_tested: the Plugins page and installing from the address
Desktop itself, and whether the tools run on its Electron Node (ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1)
whether open_setup can open the user's browser from inside DeepSeek Harness (fallback: url and fallback_code)
how the DeepSeek models use the skills; the 500-character skill description cut in the model's skill list (literature-manager is 787 characters)
whether DeepSeek Harness has a masked field for plugin settings; none was found, so keys use the setup page
deepseek-harness.engines: engines.dsh >=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0. DeepSeek Harness is a developer preview.

release_archive.requires: Node.js 22.13 or newer on the computer, except for Claude Desktop
release_archive.keys: Keys are entered through open_setup, or by double-clicking Setup AI4S.bat or Setup AI4S.command in the archive folder. scripts/onboard.mjs is not in the archive.
release_archive.note: Use the extracted folder wherever a host route names the GitHub address. Built and checked by CI; not yet tested through any host. If the latest release does not list the file, use the source route and say so.
release_archive.launchers: Setup AI4S.bat (Windows) and Setup AI4S.command (Mac) in the archive folder. Each runs: node runtime/bundle/index.mjs --setup. They need Node.js 22.13 or newer. On a Mac the first double-click may need right-click, Open.

source.locate_plugin_root: The folder that contains scripts/bootstrap.mjs and .mcp.json. Search for it; do not guess.

not_in_any_route.database-browser-runtime: Optional. Source route only, on request. Chromium (a few hundred MB, 350 to 540 MB on disk on macOS) is downloaded on first use, only after the user agrees, through the database_browser_install tool. See database-browser-runtime/README.md.
